title: Quant telemetry ingest and decisioning oracle for profile onboarding
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a telemetry ingestion + decisioning 'oracle' that automates acceptance/triage of quantization profiles (INT8/FP8/GPTQ/AWQ) for model onboarding. The oracle should combine multi-dimensional signals (accuracy deltas on eval sets, prompt-level quality regressions, latency percentiles, token-cost delta, and stability across seeds) into a single human-interpretable recommendation: accept, soft-accept (pin with guardrails), reject, or flag-for-manual-review. This ticket covers schema design, ingress pipeline, scoring functions, guardrail thresholds, and integration points with the pin registry and rollout controller.
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry schema defined and documented in Confluence with example payloads for host/edge/private deploys
Streaming ingestion pipeline implemented (Kafka topic + consumer) with at-least-once delivery and schema validation
Oracle scoring function implemented and versioned as a lightweight service (OracleScore v1) with unit tests
Automated classification (accept/soft-accept/reject/flag) emitted to pin-registry PR flow and to canary controller
Dashboard in Console shows oracle score distribution, top contributing signals, and top failing prompts
Regression detection alerts wired into SLO alerting and a daily digest to model owners
E2E smoke tests that simulate a new quant profile ingest for a sample model and verify the expected decision and rollout action
implementation_tasks: Define telemetry contract (fields, units, error codes) and publish JSON schema
Implement producer shim in onboarding harness to emit standardized telemetry
Create Kafka topic 'quant-profiles.telemetry.v1' and retention policy
Build consumer that validates payloads and writes canonical events to TimescaleDB
Implement OracleScore service: combine signals using weighted ensemble and expose REST endpoint
Integrate OracleScore decisions with pin-registry: add decision metadata and confidence score
Add canary controller hooks to respect 'soft-accept' guardrails and run staged rollouts
Instrument Console: oracle metrics, per-model score breakdown, and failing prompt examples
Write regression detection rules and PagerDuty playbook for high-confidence degradation
Add unit and integration tests for the whole pipeline
telemetry_contract: Required fields: model_name, model_version, quant_profile_id, quant_backend, metric_set (accuracy/rouge/bert_score), per_prompt_deltas (list of prompt_id, baseline_score, quant_score), latency_ms_p50/p90/p99, token_cost_delta, seed_variance, sample_size, ingest_timestamp, environment (hosted|dedicated|private). Optional: GPU_type, batch_size, sequence_length_dist
decisioning_rules: If mean quality delta > -0.5% and p99 latency delta < +10ms => accept
If mean quality delta between -0.5% and -2% AND confidence (sample_size) >= 500 => soft-accept with 3-step canary
If mean quality delta <= -2% OR top-5 prompts show catastrophic regressions => reject and flag with failing prompt examples
If token_cost_delta reduction > 20% but quality delta within -1% => add economic waiver tag for PM review
If seed_variance exceeds threshold or sample_size < 200 => flag-for-manual-review
All decisions must include OracleScore, top-3 contributing signals, and a reproducible link to eval artifacts
canary_plan: Soft-accept runs a progressive rollout: 1% traffic for 2 hours -> 5% for 4 hours -> 20% for 8 hours. At each step the canary controller evaluates the primary SLOs (accuracy band, latency p99, error-rate) and checks for drift on the top-10 prompts. Any breach triggers immediate rollback and a rollback ticket in Linear with telemetry snapshot attached.
rollback_conditions: Latency p99 increases by >25% relative to baseline during any canary step
Per-prompt worst-case degradation > 5 points (task-specific metric) on more than 3 prompts
OracleScore confidence drops below 0.6 during progressive rollout

notes: We intentionally separate OracleScore from the pin-registry to allow independent versioning of scoring logic.
OracleScore weights will be configurable per project; default weights derived from historical correlation with user-centered metrics.
Long-term: add ML-based drift detector and active learning where failing prompts are replayed against candidate quant variants to collect adversarial examples.
Keep retention of raw failing prompt text off by default; use hashed prompt plus sanitized excerpt for Console display to comply with privacy policies.
